title: Pre-SDD Entry Contract v2
description: Closed, versioned handoff from inception-pipeline to the native SDD dispatcher. Artifact references identify persisted records without embedding their content. This document validates the UNION of every supported version's vocabulary: a property or enum member added by a later bundle is legal in an instance declaring an earlier supported version, and contract_version records which bundle produced the contract rather than gating which vocabulary applies. Per-version feature gating is deliberately NOT enforced here. This schema contains no conditional keywords (no if/then/else, allOf, anyOf, oneOf, or dependentRequired) by design, so a reader can determine a property's legality from one place; every version-sensitive and cross-field invariant lives in the deterministic validator at tools/entry-contract-validator instead.

contract_version.description: The bundle version that produced this contract. The set lists every version the current bundle still accepts, newest last; the newest member must equal the inception-pipeline, shared authority, schemas, and deterministic validator bundle version. Adding a member is how a backwards-compatible extension ships without invalidating contracts written by an earlier bundle.

change_name.description: Stable kebab-case slug derived once by requirements-from-transcripts.

project.description: Stable project identifier used in artifact references.

interaction_mode.description: Whether required human decisions may be requested interactively or must use already-authorized defaults.

artifact_store_mode.description: Persistence mode selected for this change. OpenSpec paths are truthful references only, never synthetic placeholders.

complexity.description: Normalized lowercase estimate complexity; for example, Critical becomes critical.

human_review_included.description: The planned range includes human review and gate effort.

expected_checkpoints.description: Optional. Planned count of human-confirmation checkpoints, one unit per distinct human round-trip reply, over the same tiering-go-ahead-to-merge boundary the actuals record's checkpoint_count uses. This is the PLAN side of the only checkpoint pair that has both sides recorded: the actual side is checkpoint_count in sdd/{change}/actuals. sdd-time-estimation already persists it into sdd/{change}/estimate and calls it the real calendar-time driver for agent-orchestrated delivery, so omitting it here left a producer that carried the field failing the closed estimate object outright. Optional, not required: contracts written before this property existed stay valid, which is why adding it is a backwards-compatible extension of the 2.1.0 vocabulary rather than a version bump. The schema constrains the SHAPE (a non-negative integer); the deterministic validator enforces the floor of 1, which shape cannot express.

delivery_strategy.description: Resolved delivery strategy forwarded to implementation and review.

chain_strategy.description: Concrete topology when chaining is required; none otherwise. This token domain is shared with the SDD phase skills that consume it: skills/sdd-tasks/SKILL.md records it in the tasks artifact, skills/sdd-apply/SKILL.md branches on it for PR targeting, and skills/_shared/sdd-orchestrator-workflow.md defines it. A token no consumer implements would fall through every branch unguarded, so this enum must name exactly what they branch on.

size_exception.description: Planning-time and delivery-time record of a per-slice budget overrun. The object stays closed: the companion fields of every state are enumerated here and unknown keys are rejected. Which companions each state requires is a cross-field invariant enforced by the deterministic validator, not by a schema conditional.

state.description: The states divide into two kinds, and the division is the point. not-needed and approved are PRE-START PLANNING states: both are asserted before any code is written, and both are claims about the plan. not-needed asserts every planned slice is within budget; approved asserts a slice was planned over budget and that overrun was authorized up front, and so requires reason and approved_by naming who authorized it and why. granted is a DELIVERY-TIME RECORD, not a claim about the plan: it reports that a slice actually landed over budget, which is a fact about what was written that planned line counts could not have predicted, and so requires scope, changed_lines, authorized_by, and reason. This is why granted is legal precisely when the plan was within budget: it does not contradict the plan, it records what delivery revealed. MODELLING LIMIT: state holds one value, so a change that was planned over budget with an approved exception AND then overran again at delivery cannot record both facts; the delivery-time overrun would displace the planning-time authorization. That is an accepted limit of this shape, recorded here so it is not rediscovered as a surprise.

scope.description: The artifact or area whose delivery-time overrun is recorded.

changed_lines.description: Authored additions and deletions actually landed in the over-budget scope.

expected_native_next_recommendation.description: Expected nextRecommended value from the native dispatcher immediately after the validated handoff is persisted.

openspec_path.description: Normalized repository-relative path. Omit unless the artifact really exists in OpenSpec.
